# Visualizing the Chi-Square Distribution
The **Chi-square distribution** (\( \chi^2_k \)) is one of the most important distributions in statistics.  
It commonly arises when summing the squares of \(k\) independent standard normal random variables:

\[
Y = Z_1^2 + Z_2^2 + \dots + Z_k^2, \quad \text{where } Z_i \sim N(0,1)
\]

The parameter \(k\) is called the **degrees of freedom**.  
This distribution is frequently used in:
- **Goodness-of-fit tests** (e.g., the Chi-square test)
- **Testing independence** in contingency tables
- **Estimating variance** in a normal model

The **shape** of the Chi-square distribution depends strongly on the degrees of freedom:
- For small \(k\), it is **skewed right**.
- As \(k\) increases, it becomes **more symmetric**, approaching the normal distribution.

---

## Probability Density Function (PDF)

The **PDF** of the Chi-square distribution with \(k\) degrees of freedom is:

\[
f_Y(y; k) = \frac{1}{2^{k/2} \Gamma(k/2)} y^{(k/2) - 1} e^{-y/2}, \quad y > 0
\]

Here, \( \Gamma(\cdot) \) is the Gamma function.

The **mean**, **variance**, **mode**, and **median** of \(Y\) are:

\[
\text{Mean} = k, \quad
\text{Variance} = 2k, \quad
\text{Mode} = k - 2 \text{ (for } k \ge 2 \text{)}, \quad
\text{Median} \approx k \left(1 - \frac{2}{9k}\right)^3
\]

## Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF)

The **CDF** represents the probability that \(Y\) is less than or equal to some value \(y\):

\[
F_Y(y; k) = P(Y \le y) = \frac{\gamma(k/2, y/2)}{\Gamma(k/2)}
\]

where \( \gamma \) is the **lower incomplete gamma function**.  
It can also be computed numerically in R with `pchisq()`.

## The R Code

The R code below demonstrates:
1. How to **compute and plot** the PDF and CDF of the Chi-square distribution.  
2. How to **annotate the mean, median, and mode** directly on the PDF.  
3. How to create **clean, publication-ready graphics** using `ggplot2`.

```{r setup, include=TRUE}
# Load required library
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Degrees of freedom
k <- 6

# Define range of x values
x <- seq(0, 30, length.out = 400)

# Compute PDF and CDF values
pdf_vals <- dchisq(x, df = k)
cdf_vals <- pchisq(x, df = k)

# Compute statistical measures
mean_val   <- k
median_val <- qchisq(0.5, df = k)
mode_val   <- ifelse(k >= 2, k - 2, NA)

# Create data frame for plotting
df <- data.frame(x, pdf_vals, cdf_vals)

# --- Plot 1: PDF (Density Function) ---
pdf_plot <- ggplot(df, aes(x, pdf_vals)) +
  geom_line(color = "#1565C0", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_area(fill = "#BBDEFB", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = mean_val), color = "#43A047", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = median_val), color = "#FBC02D", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = mode_val), color = "#E53935", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = mean_val, y = 0.05, label = paste0("Mean = ", round(mean_val, 2)),
           color = "#43A047", hjust = -0.1, size = 4) +
  annotate("text", x = median_val, y = 0.04, label = paste0("Median = ", round(median_val, 2)),
           color = "#FBC02D", hjust = -0.1, size = 4) +
  annotate("text", x = mode_val, y = 0.03, label = paste0("Mode = ", round(mode_val, 2)),
           color = "#E53935", hjust = -0.1, size = 4) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Chi-Square (PDF) with k = ", k, " Degrees of Freedom"),
    x = "x",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

# --- Plot 2: CDF (Distribution Function) ---
cdf_plot <- ggplot(df, aes(x, cdf_vals)) +
  geom_line(color = "#8E24AA", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_area(fill = "#E1BEE7", alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Chi-Square (CDF) with k = ", k, " Degrees of Freedom"),
    x = "x",
    y = "Cumulative Probability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

# Display both plots
pdf_plot
cdf_plot
```
